NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
**Proposed intervention:** Insert a two-layer thermal interface stack — a thin pyrolytic graphite sheet (25 µm) for in-plane heat spreading followed by a silicone thermal pad (0.5 mm) for compliant contact — between the supercapacitor module base and its existing mounting bracket, using the existing bolt pattern and torque procedure.  

**Standard practice:** Automotive supercapacitor modules typically rely on natural convection and a minimal thermal interface (e.g., thermal grease or a single thin pad) at the mounting surface; no dedicated in-plane spreading layer is used.  

**Our departure:** The novelty is the **arrangement** — adding a high-conductivity graphite sheet *beneath* the module to laterally spread heat across the full bracket footprint before it crosses the compliant pad, thereby reducing the module’s steady-state temperature without active cooling or module redesign.  

**Adjacent-technique clearance:** The closest existing mitigation is a single thermal pad or grease (standard in power electronics). Our mechanism differs by inserting a *spreading layer* that exploits the bracket’s larger area, moving the thermal bottleneck from the module-to-bracket interface to the bracket-to-chassis path (which has lower resistance).  

**Failure physics attack:** Electrolyte dry-out is driven by Arrhenius-rate solvent evaporation and seal permeation; the driving variable is the **module internal temperature**. The graphite-plus-pad stack lowers that temperature by reducing the thermal resistance from cell stack to chassis, directly slowing the evaporation/permeation kinetics.

PHYSICS CHECK  
**Governing relation:** Evaporation/permeation rate ∝ exp(−Eₐ/RT_module). A reduction ΔT in T_module yields a rate reduction factor ≈ exp[(Eₐ/R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂)]. For typical Eₐ ≈ 80 kJ/mol, a 10 °C drop from 85 °C to 75 °C (358 K → 348 K) gives factor ≈ exp[80000/8.314 × (1/348 − 1/358)] ≈ 0.5 — i.e., the dry-out rate halves.  

**Magnitude verification:** The graphite sheet (κ_in-plane ≈ 1500 W/m·K, 25 µm) spreads heat over ~10× the module footprint; the silicone pad (κ ≈ 3 W/m·K, 0.5 mm) adds <0.2 K/W contact resistance. Combined stack thermal resistance ≈ 0.3 K/W vs. ~1.5 K/W for grease-only. At 5 W self-heating (typical for stop-start pulses), ΔT ≈ 6 °C lower module temperature. This yields ~2× life extension, sufficient to meet the 10% capacitance loss target at 10 years/65 °C ambient.  

**DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT:** driving variable = module internal temperature; the mechanism moves it **down** by ~6–10 °C via reduced thermal resistance to chassis; this **reduces** the failure driver (Arrhenius evaporation/permeation rate).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
| # | Item (generic class) | Source tag | Where it attaches / parameter set |
|---|----------------------|------------|-----------------------------------|
| 1 | Pyrolytic graphite sheet, 25 µm thick, in-plane κ ≥ 1500 W/m·K, commercial grade | (b) | Placed flat on the module’s base plate (entire footprint), oriented with in-plane axes parallel to bracket plane. |
| 2 | Silicone thermal interface pad, 0.5 mm thick, κ ≥ 3 W/m·K, commercial grade | (b) | Placed on top of graphite sheet, same footprint; compressed by existing mounting bolts. |
| 3 | Existing mounting bracket and bolts (stated infrastructure) | (a) | Unchanged; bolts torqued to OEM specification (procedure per service manual). |
| 4 | Installation procedure: clean module base and bracket faces with isopropyl alcohol; lay graphite sheet, then silicone pad; align module; torque bolts in cross pattern to spec. | (c) | Performed during module assembly or service; no new tools. |

*Total added stack height = 0.525 mm ≤ 1 mm budget.*

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
| Aspect | Standard practice (grease or single pad) | This intervention | Burden comparison |
|--------|------------------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Parts procurement | Thermal grease (tube) or one pad (catalog) | Two catalog sheets (graphite + pad) — both off-the-shelf, same vendor class | Same procurement class; slightly higher part count but both are stock line items. |
| Installation labor | Apply grease (messy, variable) or place one pad | Place two pre-cut sheets (clean, repeatable) | **Lower** labor variability; no curing/wipe step. |
| Tooling | None | None | Identical. |
| Added height | ~0.1 mm (grease) or 0.5 mm (pad) | 0.525 mm | Within same 1 mm envelope; no redesign of bracket or module. |
| Operational loss | None | None (passive, no duty cycle change) | Zero. |
| Maintenance | Re-grease if serviced | Replace both sheets if module removed (same interval) | Same service class. |

**Conclusion:** Same-or-lower burden class. The only added cost is a second catalog sheet (~$0.50–$1.00 per module), offset by faster, cleaner assembly.

EXECUTABLE TEST  
**Protocol:** Accelerated life test per ISO 16750-4 (temperature/humidity cycling) with electrical load profile mimicking stop-start.  
- **Samples:** 10 modules with intervention, 10 control modules (identical, grease-only interface).  
- **Conditions:** 65 °C ambient, 2.7 V/cell constant voltage, 12 V module; 10 s 300 A pulse every 30 s (cold-crank simulation), 8 h/day, 365 days/year equivalent. Accelerate by raising ambient to 85 °C (Arrhenius factor ~4×) for 2.5 years equivalent = 2190 h.  
- **Measurements:** Capacitance (1 kHz) and ESR (1 kHz) every 200 h.  
- **Pass/fail threshold:** At 2190 h (10-year equivalent), **mean capacitance loss ≤ 10%** for intervention group; control group expected >15% loss.  
- **Kill criterion:** If any intervention module exceeds 10% loss before 1500 h, the mechanism is falsified.  
- **Instruments:** Standard LCR meter (1 kHz, 1 V rms), thermal chamber, programmable load — all existing in validation lab.  
- **Duration:** 2190 h continuous (≈ 3 months).  

This test directly validates the intervention’s effectiveness on the failure metric (capacitance loss) under the stated constraints.
